candidate_relations.reason: Coccidioidomycosis is a different fungal infection and is not the cryptococcoma expected after pigeon exposure.
Primary brain tumor is the related imaging differential that led to resection of lesions that are cryptococcomas.
A neurodegenerative disease does not produce two edematous occipital mass lesions.
Dementia/confusion is the clinical manifestation of the occipital cryptococcomas, not the etiologic diagnosis.
Infection is a compatible parent but omits cryptococcoma specifically.
Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis is a different progressive encephalitis without mass-like occipital cryptococcomas.
Cerebral toxoplasmosis is a related ring-enhancing differential, not cryptococcoma in this pigeon-exposed host.
Cysticercosis is a different parasitic mass lesion from cryptococcoma.
Primary CNS lymphoma is a related enhancing-mass differential for lesions that are cryptococcomas.
Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy is a different white-matter process, not mass-forming cryptococcoma.
Metastatic brain tumor is a related two-lesion differential, not cryptococcoma.
Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease is a different rapidly progressive dementia without resectable occipital masses.
Primary CNS lymphoma is again a related mass differential rather than cryptococcoma.
Histoplasmosis is a different dimorphic fungus from cryptococcoma after pigeon exposure.
Brain tumor is the preoperative working diagnosis for mass lesions that are cryptococcomas.
Toxoplasmosis is a different opportunistic infection from cryptococcoma.
Cryptococcosis is the compatible infection family but omits the mass-forming cryptococcoma required by the reference.
Glioblastoma is a related aggressive mass differential, not cryptococcoma.
